clue.text: Clash with stoic could be academic

indicators.note: 'could be' says the letters before it might become something else if rearranged

explanation.surface: A quarrel with a stoical philosopher might be a purely academic matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholastic describes things belonging to schools and learning, the same territory covered by the adjective in the clue.

clue.text: Capital person then takes a man outside

indicators.note: the man and article are placed on the outside, wrapping the other word
one part taking another means it comes along with it

explanation.surface: Someone from the capital who later goes out with a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital person' reads like a fine fellow, but it means someone from a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: An Athenian is a native of Athens, the capital city of Greece.

clue.text: Without mother, made to autograph sketch

indicators.note: without means the following word is taken away from the next one

explanation.surface: Without his mother, a child was made to sign a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a preliminary drawing or plan, just as a sketch is.

clue.text: Classy girl leaves it in large town

indicators.note: the pronoun goes in, placed inside what remains
the girl leaving means her letters depart from the word before

explanation.surface: A posh young woman leaves something behind in a big town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classy girl' looks like one person; Classy is the word the girl leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A city is a large and important urban settlement, bigger than an ordinary town.

clue.text: Northern peer comes running round for reward

indicators.note: letters running round are moving about and change places

explanation.surface: A lord from the north comes jogging round to collect a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Recompense is payment or compensation given for effort or loss, so it is a reward.

clue.text: Part of Joe's cap is made abroad, avoiding reality

definitions.note: a phrase describing the habit; the answer is the noun for it

indicators.note: only part of the following words is needed, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: surface padding, completing the picture of the cap's origin

explanation.surface: Joe's cap was made overseas, and he would rather not face facts.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the end of Joe's and stops at the start of made.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapism is the tendency to retreat into fantasy and distraction instead of facing unpleasant truths.

clue.text: One regularly taking cannabis before a dose of medicine

indicators.note: before places the drug word ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: someone regularly taking a drug is said to be on it

explanation.surface: A habitual cannabis user taking a spoonful of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an alternate-letters signal; here being 'on' a drug means taking it regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: A potion is a liquid draught taken as a remedy, poison or drug.

clue.text: Loaded vessel's last to leave port

indicators.note: that letter is to leave, so it is removed from the first word
last points to the final letter of the vessel word

explanation.surface: A laden ship is the last to leave the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the L off LADEN leaves ADEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a seaport city in Yemen, long a major harbour at the mouth of the Red Sea.

clue.text: Revolver produced by a pyrotechnist?

parts.note: surface: a handgun with a rotating cylinder
setter's reading: a firework maker's product that spins round when lit

explanation.walkthrough: Revolver suggests a gun, but a fireworks maker's revolver is the spinning firework pinned to a post.
explanation.definitionFit: This firework, named after Saint Catherine's martyrdom wheel, rotates as it burns, so it literally revolves.

clue.text: Coming from Wales, rows with world entertainer!

indicators.note: the answer comes from these words, which are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A Welsh performer who quarrels with the whole world.
explanation.definitionFit: This circus or street performer is an entertainer who passes a blade down the throat to amaze audiences.

clue.text: Old Turkish governor gets to pose in it, being fat

definitions.note: a gerund phrase for the state the noun names

indicators.note: the posing word goes in, inside the governor

parts.note: a bey was an Ottoman provincial governor
to pose for a portrait is to sit

explanation.surface: An Ottoman official poses for a portrait, showing off his corpulence.
explanation.walkthrough: A bey was a provincial governor in the Ottoman Empire, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Obesity is the condition of carrying excessive body weight, the state of a person who is very overweight.

clue.text: Praise tank I love working around

indicators.note: around says the last two pieces wrap themselves round the first ones

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
a vat is a large tank
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone praises a tank they love that is still running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love working' together go around the tank and I, one piece each side.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is a burst of applause from an audience, an enthusiastic public expression of approval.

clue.text: Repugnant article about romance

indicators.note: about means the article goes round the other word

parts.note: to romance is to tell fanciful untruths

explanation.surface: A hostile newspaper piece about someone's love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romance' looks like a love story; as a verb it means to invent stories, so a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alien to a person is contrary to their nature, hence distasteful or offensive to them.

clue.text: Cover note I'd written out is given a heading

parts.note: a cap covers the head or a bottle

indicators.note: written out suggests setting the letters down afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cover note written out in full is given a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A captioned picture or article has a title or explanatory heading attached above or beneath it.

clue.text: Frequency usual on famous loch

parts.note: Loch Ness in Scotland, home of the legendary monster

explanation.surface: How often the usual sightings happen on Scotland's best-known lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Commonness is the quality of occurring often, so it amounts to how frequently something happens.

clue.text: Liquid rises — could leak

indicators.note: something liquid flows and changes shape, so the following letters are fluid

explanation.surface: As fluid rises it may seep out of its container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid' and 'leak' make a plumbing scene, but 'could' is fodder and 'leak' is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A leak is an unauthorised release of secret information, which is a kind of revealing to the public.

clue.text: Instructions once written on tablets?

parts.note: surface: directions printed on a pill packet
setter's reading: stone slabs carried down Mount Sinai by Moses

explanation.walkthrough: Tablets suggests pills with dosage directions; the stone tablets of the Bible bore God's laws.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical laws given to Moses were inscribed on two stone slabs, as orders for the Israelites.

clue.text: Dungarees and everything in sets of six deliveries

indicators.note: in places the everything word inside the cricket sets

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled

explanation.surface: A cricketer's work clothes and kit spread over a long innings.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Overalls are protective trousers with a bib and straps, which is what dungarees are.

clue.text: Badly burnt individual's colour

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so the next word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: what is an individual's is their own

explanation.surface: A sunburnt person's skin tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut-brown is a warm shade like a ripe hazelnut shell, a hue often used of tanned skin.

clue.text: Patient takes second part from dish

indicators.note: the patient takes in, holding the next letter inside

parts.note: a doctor's patient is a case
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A hospital patient picks a second helping from the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A doctor speaks of a patient as a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a slow-cooked stew, and also the lidded pot it is made in, so a dish either way.

clue.text: Order string

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sequence in which things are arranged
second meaning: a succession of related things, like a string of wins

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a command to buy twine; both words are nouns for a sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A series is a number of similar things following one another, which fits both a set order and a run of events.

clue.text: Praise given to student once ahead

indicators.note: ahead puts the former-times word at the front

parts.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Praise once heaped on a pupil who got ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate British learner drivers display, so it stands for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to commend enthusiastically, a verb meaning to speak highly of something.

clue.text: See when one enters with little trouble

indicators.note: enters means the pair goes inside the see

explanation.surface: Look at the moment someone comes in without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is the crossword's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily means without difficulty or effort, so done with hardly any bother at all.

clue.text: Ruin act, removing veil

indicators.note: read as re-moving, moving the letters about again

explanation.surface: A stripper's routine is spoilt when the veil comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removing' reads as taking something off, but split as re-moving it signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain is a screen of fabric that hangs down to conceal something, as a veil does.

clue.text: Monk may wear this on cold hooter!

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece on another sits above it, so first

parts.note: abbreviation for cold on a tap

explanation.surface: A monk pulls something over his red nose in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooter is British slang for nose, which the surface suggests; here it is the bird that hoots.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is the large hood of a monk's habit, worn over the head.

clue.text: They write about street restaurants

indicators.note: about means the writing things go round the street abbreviation

explanation.surface: Critics write reviews of the restaurants along a street.
explanation.walkthrough: Biro is the everyday British name for a ballpoint pen, so pens are what write.
explanation.definitionFit: Bistros are small, informal eateries, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Smile broadly, accepting a medal

indicators.note: accepting means the medal takes the article inside

explanation.surface: Someone grins widely on receiving a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: The BEM, the British Empire Medal, is a UK honour for civil or military service.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to grin radiantly, a verb for a wide happy smile.
